source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Somerset, New Jersey campus publishes 23 MW of IT capacity, second in the state, and it is one of only five New Jersey data centers that disclose power at all.

The 23 MW sits inside 185,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common colocation baseline, that space holds roughly 575 racks. At 80 kW per rack, a denser training configuration, it holds roughly 290. The rack count depends entirely on the density assumption, and the record does not say which one applies.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data centers. Five operators publish power figures, and those five total 111.3 MW, of which Somerset is 20.7 percent. Published capacity is a floor on the state's inventory, not a measure of it, because most mapped facilities disclose nothing. The same caution applies to Somerset: no certifications are published, so nothing in the record qualifies the campus for any specific workload.

What the data does not contain is what would settle the AI question. There is no address, no coordinates, no utility or interconnection detail, no tenant list, and no measured consumption. A 23 MW campus is modest against hyperscale AI clusters, and whether it serves inference, smaller training jobs, or neither cannot be determined from published figures. The suitability score of 64 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
